article_notes: 86 dogs with uncomplicated B. rossi babesiosis (capillary smear, PCR confirmed) at Onderstepoort (OVAH); complicated cases were excluded. The only severity split is transfused (n = 32; the authors call them the more anaemic group) vs non-transfused (n = 54), with CBCs at presentation, Day 1, Day 3 and Day 6 after diminazene treatment (presentation samples taken at diagnosis; later samples after treatment and, in transfused dogs, after transfusion). Group sizes per day are in Table 1 (presentation 31 vs 53). Outcome (4 deaths, 2 per group) did not differ between groups (P = 0.62); deaths were too few for any marker comparison by outcome. Group comparisons of HCT, ARC and leukocytes use multiple regression with age and treatment group; per-group medians are mostly shown only in box plots (Figs 1-9), so values are given where the text prints them. Table 3 rows for Day 3 and Day 6 (neutrophilia, neutropenia, concurrent neutrophilia, left shift by group) were not recorded as separate rows: they are descriptive, after treatment and transfusion. Effects of age on haematology and of whole blood vs packed cells are not severity comparisons and were not extracted.

severity_definitions.label: transfused vs non-transfused dogs
severity_definitions.definition: Blood transfusion given at the attending clinician's decision, as a guideline when PCV < 15 % and also depending on clinical status (e.g. collapse). Dogs needing a transfusion that was refused for cost were excluded, as were all complicated cases. The authors treat the transfused group as the more severely anaemic group.
severity_definitions.quote: As a general guideline, dogs with PCV of <15 % were transfused, but in many cases the clinical status of the dog ( e.g. collapsed vs non-collapsed) played a role in decision-making.
